title: Finite periodic Q3 split Gibbs/KMS source and shape stress
question: On the registered finite periodic control graphs (one bond, square and 2x3 grid), do all source sites retain the finite Gibbs stationarity and analytic KMS mesh-decrease pattern for both split orders, signs and beta values, and how does the residual change with degree/shape?

model.observable_pair: A_x=exp(i a q_x/hbar), B_x=exp(i a p_x/hbar) for every site x
model.gibbs_state: rho_beta=exp(-beta H)/Tr(exp(-beta H)) for the same finite periodic-control H
model.kms_boundary: R_x=Tr(rho A_x alpha^S_t(B_x))-Tr(rho alpha^S_{t+i beta hbar}(B_x) A_x)
model.shape_scope: bond2, square4 and grid2x3 are finite periodic-control graphs; no thermodynamic torus limit is inferred.

adversarial_review.check: The three explicit edge sets and all source sites are checked; the finite controls are not labelled an infinite periodic torus.
The alpha convention uses t+i beta hbar at every source and both real-time signs.
Complex products use reverse factor order and -z for their inverse, not a complex adjoint.
Only d=3 is admitted and a positive [H,H_onsite] witness is required for every graph.
All finite sites are measured and boundary-free degree effects are reported; no source-uniform limit is inferred.
Per-source coarse/fine decreases are checked on two mesh values only; no analytic uniform Trotter rate is claimed.
The independent lane rebuilds the periodic graph matrices and residuals without importing the primary script.
Lean R247 checks the exact rational finite Gibbs normalization/commutation fixture; dense periodic matrices remain Python evidence.
Finite periodic controls do not prove compatible exhaustion embeddings, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS identification, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A.

lean_crosscheck.role: R247 checks exact rational finite Gibbs normalization/commutation; Python checks periodic-control matrices and source-wise KMS residuals.

qft_interface.closed: Exact finite-H Gibbs controls and source-wise split stationarity/KMS residuals are reproduced on the registered bond2, square4 and grid2x3 controls for both split orders, signs, beta values and meshes.
qft_interface.open: Degree/shape finite ranges do not supply a source-, volume-, cutoff- or beta-uniform analytic rate, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, common core, exhaustion independence, one common alpha, Hamiltonian-to-OS/KMS quotient, gap, continuum or physical TECT closure.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: Auxiliary C6/Q3 finite evidence only; no heat_root_incidence, canonical A1/R-192 production owner, physical-empty reference, Sector-A closure or Pre-A closure is supplied.

next_action: Use the degree/shape residual range to target a periodic common-core estimate with explicit degree constants; if those constants grow with cutoff or volume, record the route-local obstruction before common-alpha promotion.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite d=3 periodic-control Q3 KMS diagnostic. It is not a thermodynamic torus theorem, source-uniformity theorem, common-alpha construction or QFT/Clay result.
no_overclaim: All-site finite periodic residuals and their mesh decrease do not identify one thermodynamic Q3 dynamics or close OS/KMS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A gates.
